```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("vanErp_2016_everolimus"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("vanErp_2016_everolimus"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s40262-016-0414-3> (open access, PMC5069307)

van Erp et al. fitted a semi-physiological model to whole-blood everolimus
concentrations, but parameterised it in plasma terms: each whole-blood
observation was converted to plasma with its paired hematocrit and the fixed
85:15 erythrocyte:plasma concentration ratio (Eq. 1). Absorption runs through
a depot and four transit compartments into a well-stirred liver compartment.
The liver's plasma flow, `QH * (1 - Ht)`, and the unbound intrinsic clearance
`fu * CLint` set the hepatic extraction ratio. Drug that escapes extraction
reaches a two-compartment plasma disposition system. The unbound plasma
concentration drives a previously published S6K1-inhibition Imax model, which
the paper used only for simulation.

# Population

Seventy-three adults (51 female, 22 male; median age 62 years, range 37-80;
median weight 73.2 kg, range 45-105) came from two Dutch studies. Forty-one had
progressive thyroid cancer (THYRRAD phase II) and 32 had metastatic breast
cancer (INPRES phase IV). All received everolimus 10 mg once daily (10-15 mg
per occasion). Median hematocrit was 38% (range 25-49.7%), and 947 whole-blood
concentrations were analysed (van Erp 2016 Table 1). Each patient was sampled
on two occasions: days 1 and 15 in THYRRAD, days 14 and 35 in INPRES.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("vanErp_2016_everolimus")()$population`.

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lmat` (MAT) | 0.544 h | Table 2 |
| `lclint` (CLint/F) | 198 L/h | Table 2 |
| `lvc` (V3/F) | 207 L | Table 2 |
| `lq` (Q) | 72.1 L/h | Table 2 |
| `lvp` (V4/F) | 485 L | Table 2 |
| `lqh` (QH) | 90 L/h, fixed | Methods, Structural Pharmacokinetic Model |
| `lvliver` (Vliver) | 1 L, fixed | Methods, Structural Pharmacokinetic Model |
| `lfu` (fu) | 0.27, fixed | Table 2; Methods Eq. 4 |
| `rbc_plasma_ratio` | 85/15, fixed | Table 2; Methods Eq. 1 (4.667 = 85/15 - 1) |
| `ntr` (number of transit compartments) | 4, fixed | Results, Estimation Results; Fig. 1 |
| `imax_s6k1` | 97 %, fixed | Methods Eq. 6 (Tanaka 2008) |
| `ic50_s6k1` | 0.05 ng/mL, fixed | Methods Eq. 6 (Tanaka 2008) |
| `etalclint`, `etalvc` | 38.9 %, 36.1 % CV; correlation 0.347 | Table 2 |
| `etalmat` | 62.0 % CV | Table 2 |
| `etalfu` | 3 % CV, fixed | Table 2 |
| `etaiov_fdepot_1`, `etaiov_fdepot_2` | 15.2 % CV | Table 2 (inter-occasion variability on F1) |
| `propSd` | 26.0 % | Table 2 |
| `ktr = (n + 1) / MAT` | n/a | Methods Eq. 2 |
| `qhp = QH * (1 - Ht)` | n/a | Methods Eq. 3 |
| `eh = CLint * fu / (qhp + CLint * fu)` | n/a | Methods Eq. 4 |
| `clh = eh * qhp` | n/a | Methods Eq. 5 |
| `k20`, `k23`, `k32`, `k34`, `k43` | n/a | Methods, rate-constant list after Fig. 1 |
| Compartment layout (depot, transits, liver, central, peripheral) | n/a | Fig. 1 |
| `Cblood = Cc * (1 + 4.667 * Ht)` | n/a | Methods Eq. 1 |
| `Cu = fu * Cc` | n/a | Methods, Structural Pharmacokinetic Model |
| `s6k1_inhibition = Imax * Cu / (IC50 + Cu)` | n/a | Methods Eq. 6 |

# Typical-value steady state (Figure 4)

The paper's Figure 4 shows the typical patient at steady state on 10 mg once
daily, at a hematocrit of 20% and of 45%. The simulation below gives 30 daily
doses and plots the last dosing interval.

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("vanErp_2016_everolimus")
mod_typical <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)

dose_times <- seq(0, 29 * 24, by = 24)
obs_times <- 29 * 24 + seq(0, 24, by = 0.05)

make_typical <- function(hct, id) {
  dplyr::bind_rows(
    data.frame(time = dose_times, evid = 1, amt = 10, cmt = "depot"),
    data.frame(time = obs_times, evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(id = id, HCT = hct, OCC = 1, hct_grp = paste0(hct, "% hematocrit")) |>
    dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}
ev_typical <- dplyr::bind_rows(make_typical(20, 1L), make_typical(45, 2L))

sim_typical <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typical, events = ev_typical, keep = "hct_grp") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - 29 * 24)
```

```{r figure-4, fig.height = 7, fig.width = 6}
sim_typical |>
  dplyr::select(tad, hct_grp,
    `Whole blood (ng/mL)` = Cblood,
    `Plasma (ng/mL)` = Cc,
    `S6K1 inhibition (%)` = s6k1_inhibition
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-c(tad, hct_grp)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(name = factor(name, levels = c("Whole blood (ng/mL)", "Plasma (ng/mL)", "S6K1 inhibition (%)"))) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, value, colour = hct_grp)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(~name, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 24, by = 4)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose (h)", y = NULL, colour = NULL,
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of van Erp 2016 (10 mg QD, typical patient, steady state)."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The peak and trough values below were read by the maintainers off the
published Figure 4 and are approximate (about +/- 1 ng/mL and +/- 0.3%).

```{r figure-4-check}
fig4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~hct_grp, ~quantity, ~published,
  "20% hematocrit", "Whole-blood peak (ng/mL)", 48,
  "45% hematocrit", "Whole-blood peak (ng/mL)", 68,
  "20% hematocrit", "Whole-blood trough (ng/mL)", 7.8,
  "45% hematocrit", "Whole-blood trough (ng/mL)", 14,
  "20% hematocrit", "Plasma peak (ng/mL)", 24.7,
  "45% hematocrit", "Plasma peak (ng/mL)", 22,
  "20% hematocrit", "Plasma trough (ng/mL)", 4.0,
  "45% hematocrit", "Plasma trough (ng/mL)", 4.4,
  "20% hematocrit", "S6K1 inhibition peak (%)", 96.2,
  "45% hematocrit", "S6K1 inhibition peak (%)", 96.2,
  "20% hematocrit", "S6K1 inhibition trough (%)", 92.8,
  "45% hematocrit", "S6K1 inhibition trough (%)", 93.1
)
sim_fig4 <- sim_typical |>
  dplyr::group_by(hct_grp) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Whole-blood peak (ng/mL)` = max(Cblood),
    `Whole-blood trough (ng/mL)` = Cblood[tad == 24],
    `Plasma peak (ng/mL)` = max(Cc),
    `Plasma trough (ng/mL)` = Cc[tad == 24],
    `S6K1 inhibition peak (%)` = max(s6k1_inhibition),
    `S6K1 inhibition trough (%)` = s6k1_inhibition[tad == 24],
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-hct_grp, names_to = "quantity", values_to = "simulated")
fig4_cmp <- dplyr::left_join(fig4, sim_fig4, by = c("hct_grp", "quantity")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated - published) / published)
fig4_cmp |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Hematocrit" = hct_grp, "Quantity" = quantity,
    "Figure 4 (digitised)" = published, "Simulated" = simulated,
    "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = c(0, 0, 1, 2, 1))

# Deterministic typical-value solve against a digitised figure: every value
# within the digitisation error. A wrong CLint, fu, V or hematocrit mapping
# moves these by far more than 6%.
stopifnot(all(abs(fig4_cmp$pct_diff) < 6))
```

# PKNCA and the closed-form exposure check

When the whole dose enters the liver compartment, the well-stirred model makes
the apparent oral plasma clearance equal to the unbound intrinsic clearance:
`CL_H / (1 - E_H) = fu * CLint`. The steady-state plasma AUC over one dosing
interval is therefore `Dose / (fu * CLint)` = 10 mg / (0.27 x 198 L/h) =
187.1 ng*h/mL, whatever the hematocrit. Hematocrit changes how much of that
exposure reaches whole blood, not the plasma AUC. PKNCA computes the
interval AUC on the typical-value profiles.

```{r pknca}
sim_nca <- sim_typical |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(hct_grp, id, tad, Cc, Cblood) |>
  dplyr::rename(time = tad)

dose_nca <- sim_nca |>
  dplyr::distinct(hct_grp, id) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = 10)

intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 24,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
)

nca_plasma <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cc ~ time | hct_grp + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, amt ~ time | hct_grp + id),
  intervals = intervals
))
nca_blood <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  PKNCA::PKNCAconc(sim_nca, Cblood ~ time | hct_grp + id),
  PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_nca, amt ~ time | hct_grp + id),
  intervals = intervals
))

nca_tab <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(nca_plasma) |> dplyr::mutate(matrix = "Plasma"),
  as.data.frame(nca_blood) |> dplyr::mutate(matrix = "Whole blood")
) |>
  dplyr::select(matrix, hct_grp, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

nca_tab |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Matrix" = matrix, "Hematocrit" = hct_grp,
    "Cmax (ng/mL)" = cmax, "Tmax (h)" = tmax, "Cmin (ng/mL)" = cmin,
    "AUC0-24 (ng*h/mL)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical-value steady-state NCA (10 mg QD).")

auc_closed <- 10 / (0.27 * 198) * 1000
auc_plasma <- nca_tab$auclast[nca_tab$matrix == "Plasma"]
auc_plasma
auc_closed
# Same drawn parameters on both sides (typical values), so this is pure
# numerical error from the 0.05 h trapezoid grid: keep the bound tight.
stopifnot(all(abs(auc_plasma / auc_closed - 1) < 0.005))
```

Neither the paper nor its figures report an NCA table, so there is no
published NCA to compare with. The closed-form AUC check above and the
Table 3 trough comparison below take its place.

# Stochastic steady-state troughs (Table 3)

Table 3 of the paper summarises steady-state pre-dose concentrations and S6K1
inhibition for 1000 virtual patients on two occasions at each hematocrit. The
virtual cohort below has 200 patients per hematocrit arm. Each patient takes
10 mg once daily for 28 days: days 0-13 are occasion 1 and days 14-27
occasion 2. One trough is read at the end of each occasion. Table 3's column
headers print the unit as ng/L, which is a misprint for ng/mL (= ug/L, the
unit of Figure 4 and of the assay ranges).

```{r stochastic}
make_cohort <- function(n, hct, id_offset) {
  ids <- id_offset + seq_len(n)
  dose <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = seq(0, 27 * 24, by = 24)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 1, amt = 10, cmt = "depot")
  obs <- expand.grid(id = ids, time = c(14 * 24 - 0.01, 28 * 24 - 0.01)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
  dplyr::bind_rows(dose, obs) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      HCT = hct,
      OCC = ifelse(time < 14 * 24, 1, 2),
      hct_grp = paste0(hct, "% hematocrit")
    ) |>
    dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}
ev_sto <- dplyr::bind_rows(make_cohort(200, 20, 0L), make_cohort(200, 45, 200L))
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(unique(ev_sto[, c("id", "hct_grp")])$id))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(2016)
sim_sto <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_sto, keep = "hct_grp") |>
  as.data.frame()

summ <- function(x) {
  sprintf("%.3g (%.3g-%.3g)", median(x), quantile(x, 0.05), quantile(x, 0.95))
}
sto_tab <- sim_sto |>
  dplyr::group_by(hct_grp) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Whole blood (ng/mL)` = summ(Cblood),
    `Plasma (ng/mL)` = summ(Cc),
    `S6K1 inhibition (%)` = summ(s6k1_inhibition),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(source = "Simulated, median (90% PI)")
pub_tab <- tibble::tribble(
  ~hct_grp, ~`Whole blood (ng/mL)`, ~`Plasma (ng/mL)`, ~`S6K1 inhibition (%)`,
  "20% hematocrit", "7.85 (3.31-18.7)", "4.06 (1.71-9.65)", "92.8 (87.5-95.2)",
  "45% hematocrit", "14.0 (6.19-30.6)", "4.51 (2.00-9.86)", "93.2 (88.9-95.2)"
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(source = "van Erp 2016 Table 3")
dplyr::bind_rows(pub_tab, sto_tab) |>
  dplyr::arrange(hct_grp, source) |>
  dplyr::rename("Hematocrit" = hct_grp, "Source" = source) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Steady-state trough concentrations and S6K1 inhibition.")
```

The simulated summaries are individual predictions without residual error.
Table 3 describes simulated exposure rather than observations, and the
published 90% prediction intervals match these predictions better than they
match predictions with the 26% residual error added.

```{r stochastic-check}
pub_med <- tibble::tribble(
  ~hct_grp, ~Cblood_pub, ~Cc_pub, ~s6k1_pub,
  "20% hematocrit", 7.85, 4.06, 92.8,
  "45% hematocrit", 14.0, 4.51, 93.2
)
med_cmp <- sim_sto |>
  dplyr::group_by(hct_grp) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Cblood_sim = median(Cblood), Cc_sim = median(Cc),
    s6k1_sim = median(s6k1_inhibition), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::left_join(pub_med, by = "hct_grp")
med_cmp
# Centre of a random cohort, not its extremes: a mis-transcribed clearance or
# hematocrit mapping shifts these medians by tens of percent.
stopifnot(
  all(abs(med_cmp$Cblood_sim / med_cmp$Cblood_pub - 1) < 0.15),
  all(abs(med_cmp$Cc_sim / med_cmp$Cc_pub - 1) < 0.15),
  all(abs(med_cmp$s6k1_sim - med_cmp$s6k1_pub) < 1.5)
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

- **IIV scale.** Table 2 reports inter-individual and inter-occasion
  variability as CV%. These are converted to log-normal variances with
  `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`. The correlation of 0.347 between CLint and V3
  becomes a covariance of `0.347 * sqrt(omega^2_CLint * omega^2_V3)`.
- **Occasions.** Inter-occasion variability on F1 is encoded as two
  occasions sharing one variance, matching the two sampling occasions per
  patient in the source studies and the two simulated occasions of Table 3.
  A simulation that does not model occasions can set `OCC = 1` throughout.
- **Bioavailability.** The paper reports apparent (`/F`) parameters, so the
  typical bioavailability is 1 and only its between-occasion variability is
  carried. `f(depot)` scales the dose before it enters the transit chain.
- **Unbound-fraction variability.** Table 2 lists a fixed 3% IIV on fu. It is
  kept as a fixed random effect on `fu`, which feeds both the hepatic
  extraction ratio and the unbound concentration.
- **Residual error.** The 26% residual error is encoded as proportional on
  the observed whole-blood concentration (`Cblood`). The paper does not say
  whether it is additive on the log scale or proportional; at 26% the two
  behave almost the same.
- **Observation names.** `Cc` is the plasma concentration (the model's
  central compartment is plasma), `Cblood` is the whole-blood concentration
  that was measured, and `Cu` is the unbound plasma concentration. Hematocrit
  `HCT` is supplied in percent and divided by 100 inside the model, since
  Eqs. 1 and 3 use the volume fraction.
- **S6K1 model.** The Imax model (Imax 97%, IC50 0.05 ng/mL unbound) comes from
  Tanaka et al. (J Clin Oncol 2008) and is reproduced as the paper used it in
  its simulations. It was not fitted to these patients, and like the paper it
  has no variability of its own.
- **Not reproduced.** Figure 3 (prediction-corrected VPC) needs the
  original dataset and is not reproduced. No erratum for this article was
  found as of 2026-11-25.
